Definition: probably akin to πετάννυμι (to spread; and thus apparently allied to G4072 through the idea of expansion, and to 4429 through that of flattening; compare G3961); to fold, i.e. furl a scroll:--close.
BiblicalUsage: Ptysso means to fold, to roll up. It appears once, in the synagogue at Nazareth: Jesus closed the book, and He gave it again to the minister, and sat down, and the eyes of all them that were in the synagogue were fastened on Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe He closed the book because the prophecy was finished: He had read of Himself, and now He sat down to do what was written.
